PullRequest.Title: sessions: keep new chat pills opaque over backgrounds
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- Give new-session bottom-row controls an opaque secondary-control surface when a chat background is active.
- Preserve the themed hover treatment over that surface.
- Cover the production `.chat-view-new` ancestry with a focused regression test.

## Screenshots

### Dark

![New chat background pills in the dark theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3eecad8e-73e9-4d14-868d-9bf76f617033)

### Light

![New chat background pills in the light theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/47516ebc-e008-4c44-9a46-cf988b9a7311)

## Testing

- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/media/chatWidget.css`
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatView.test.ts`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatView.test.ts --grep "keeps background-image composer controls on complete opaque surfaces"`

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the new-session composer with a configured chat background, then hover its bottom-row session/repository/status controls.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Construction creates one bottom control row; browser style resolution and paint must complete before the composer is visually ready. Hover restyles and repaints the hovered control. No asynchronous application work is added to this critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with the finite number of action labels in the single new-chat bottom row (session controls, repository configuration, and status actions), not chat-history length or list-row count. Hover affects one label at a time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work is reached by the CSS change. Style matching and painting run in the browser rendering pipeline; controls are created synchronously as one bounded toolbar row, not scheduled concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The stylesheet is loaded through the existing path; the change introduces no application cache, cache key, cache miss, or coalescing behavior. Cold and warm behavior differ only by normal browser stylesheet/rendering caches already present before the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the diff broadens existing background/border/color styling to production `.chat-view-new` descendants and adds a hover paint. High confidence it does not add layout reads, animation, collection-wide work, retained state, or an expensive external boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact paint cost of the opaque color plus constant linear-gradient layer is browser/theme dependent and was not benchmarked, but the affected node count is small and bounded and the same treatment already applies to equivalent controls under the existing `.chat-view` ancestry.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Before the diff, production `.chat-view-new` bottom controls received only the base surface plus a border; after it they receive the same static layered surface already used by `.chat-view` controls. The bounded extra paint on a handful of controls, and one hovered control, does not establish user-visible latency or dropped frames.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced the changed selector through new-chat control construction and existing equivalent chat-view styling. The only production change is bounded static/hover paint on a small toolbar row; test changes add one fixture node and one computed-style read only during the focused test. No actionable performance regression or regression fix was found.
